gaps.one_line_takeaway: For our case, the 1.3 to 1.7 point gain from old-only replay looks like extra practice on old skills rather than transfer from the new skills (mixing in new rows cut it by about 1 point), so call it replay practice and claim backward transfer only if new-skill training beats a matched-steps old-only arm; no paper I found reports that exact control.

critic:
1. Parameter-regularization consolidation (EWC, LwF) - a replay-free control that tests whether replay is needed at all, and a complement to it - Kirkpatrick et al. 2017, PNAS, "Overcoming catastrophic forgetting in neural networks"
2. Interference-targeted or prioritized replay selection - picks which day's finds and old items to rehearse instead of a random mix, which could cut overnight updates - Aljundi et al. 2019, NeurIPS, "Online Continual Learning with Maximally Interfered Retrieval"
3. Architectural isolation (adapters or orthogonal subspaces) - protects old skills by construction, so new skills can be learned without touching old weights - Wang et al. 2023, EMNLP Findings, "Orthogonal Subspace Learning for Language Model Continual Learning"
4. Synaptic homeostasis (global downscaling during sleep) - a biological model for an overnight scaling or weight-decay step that frees capacity - Tononi & Cirelli 2014, Neuron, "Sleep and the Price of Plasticity"
5. Complementary learning systems (fast episodic store plus slow cortical learner) - the direct template for a day buffer plus overnight consolidation split - McClelland, McNaughton & O'Reilly 1995, Psychological Review
